messages:
marta: heads up — just saw a customer report where a long streaming response got routed mid-stream during a canary handoff and ended up charging the user twice for a tool call.

vikram: ugh. any logs? is this the reconnect path we patched last quarter or something new?

marta: attaching a trimmed log snippet i pulled from the router:
```
[2026-03-20T15:12:03Z] route-inbound id=abc123 session_id=ses-9a3 route=old-variant ledger_entry=ldr-77
[2026-03-20T15:12:18Z] handoff id=abc123 session_id=ses-9a3 -> route=new-variant new_ledger=ldr-78
[2026-03-20T15:12:19Z] toolcall start id=toolcall-555 session_header=X-Session-Id=ses-9a3 request_id=req-999 ledger_ref=ldr-78
[2026-03-20T15:12:19Z] toolcall start id=toolcall-555 session_header=X-Session-Id=ses-9a3 request_id=req-999 ledger_ref=ldr-77
```
Looks like both ledgers got a start event for the same toolcall.

sophie: interesting — router emitted a handoff but downstream services still had the old ledger ref and also recorded the call. we treat toolcalls as non-idempotent unless they include an idempotency key. do we have one here? marta: no, upstream client doesn't set idempotency-key for streaming tool calls; we rely on session+request ids to dedupe.

jeff: so the same request_id was seen twice but with different ledger_refs. dedupe logic probably keyed by (session_id, request_id) but we also attach ledger_ref when committing charge, so both ledger rows were created.

kevin: if the router changes ledger_ref mid-flight we should either forward the original ledger_ref to the new route OR emit a single "handoff" event that signals downstream to reconcile and avoid creating a new charge. which is simpler to ship?

vikram: forward original ledger_ref is smallest change in router: add header X-Original-Ledger: ldr-77 on handoff. downstream billing consumer will prefer original if present. downside: makes leaky abstraction between router and ledger service.

sophie: alternative: make the billing service idempotent on (session_id, request_id) only — ignore ledger_ref when deduping. that seems safer but might require a small migration to ensure no old entries slip through.

marta: quick experiments: patched router locally to forward X-Original-Ledger and replayed the sequence. single ledger row created. but still worried about edge when old backend already emitted a start and new backend also emits start within milliseconds — race.

jeff: can we emit a transient "rollback" event when we detect a duplicate start? billing could reconcile and mark one as provisional and then drop provisional on confirm from original ledger.

kevin: UX/console note: we should show these provisional vs final charges in the billing console so support can explain to customers. add a small flag on ledger rows: provisional=true|false and a timeline that shows handoff events.

sophie: actionable plan proposal:
- short-term: router forwards X-Original-Ledger on handoff (patch + smoke tests) — low risk
- mid-term: billing dedupe solely on (session_id, request_id) and ignore ledger_ref for idempotency, plus add provisional flag
- long-term: routing UX change to drain long-lived streams during canary (configurable) and a handoff telemetry event emitted to ledger with reason

marta: i'll open a canary patch for the router and a small billing DB migration PR. anyone want to co-owner the billing change?

jeff: i can take the billing dedupe PR. will add tests for races where two start events arrive within 200ms.

vikram: pls add a quick metric: counter for "duplicate_toolcall_by_handoff" under platform.metrics so we can watch after rollout.

platform-bot: deploy-bot: new patch marta/router-forward-ledger opened (#4321). CI: running.

kevin: one more note — let's also update the console docs for the rollout guide: suggest a drain window for streaming clients and flags to enable automatic handoff reconciliation.

marta: thanks all. i'll post the PR links when CI passes and schedule a 30min sync if we hit flaky test failures. :thumbsup:
